name: Topics in Computational Social Choice
description:
”Social Choice Theory” deals with methods for collective decision-making. Beyond classical applications such as voting procedures, these methods have found applications in various areas of computer science. This course builds on the foundations introduced in IN2229. It covers three major models that have attracted significant research interest in recent years:
– Fair Division: cake cutting, allocating indivisible goods, house allocation problem
– Public Goods Allocation: participatory budgeting, budget aggregation, multi-winner approval voting, Lindahl equilibrium 
– Probabilistic Social Choice: SSB utilities, maximal lotteries, random dictatorship theorem, random assignment
In each of these topics, the emphasis is on mathematically rigorous, provable results.
prerequisites:
It is expected that students are already familiar with some of the foundations of preference models and axiomatic analysis done in computational social choice.
– Algorithmic Game Theory (IN2239)
– Computational Social Choice (IN2229)
– Introduction to Theory of Computation (IN0015)
